messages:
marta: Quick design question — compact token-breakdown card vs expanded line-items on the Usage page. Trying to decide default for org-scoped view. Screenshot attached (mock). Thoughts?

kevin: my 2¢: org view should be high-level. compact card with totals + tiny sparkline. expand on click to show projects. keeps noise down for execs. :chart_with_upwards_trend: 

sam: Agreed on high-level default, but two caveats: 1) we need clear affordance to switch to project-level. 2) billing admins often want invoice links right next to totals — don't hide download behind another click.

jess: UX nits — in compact mode, make the token breakdown column readable for screen readers. Right now the visual abbreviations (P / C) are unclear. Propose: aria-labels "Prompt tokens" and "Completion tokens" and a tooltip.

marta: Good call, jess. For abbreviations we can show full label on hover and keep the short form visually. Does that satisfy density constraints?

kevin: yes. Also add a subtle chevron to indicate expansion. Keyboard users should be able to press Enter/Space to expand. aria-expanded attr.

aria: billing-bot posted an update: "New CSV export is available at /billing/export?scope=org — includes prompt/completion/total and invoice_id."

marta: Cool — where should the CSV/invoice CTA live in compact card? inline next to total or in a small actions overflow?

sam: Inline next to total would be most discoverable. But mobile screens are tight. Maybe inline on desktop, overflow on mobile.

jess: Accessibility: if we put it inline, ensure focus order doesn't skip it. Use logical DOM order: total -> download -> expand. Also visible focus ring.

kevin: UX trade: inline download increases width; overflow hides it. Can we make a responsive rule: >= 960px show inline, else collapse into kebab menu?

marta: That works. Also want to revisit token breakdown granularity: show Prompt / Completion / Fine-tune cost? Or hide fine-tune unless >0.

sam: Hide unless non-zero. Most orgs don't use fine-tune and it adds cognitive load.

jess: Copy tweak for invoice link: change label to "Download invoice (PDF)" instead of just "Invoice" — clearer. Also tooltip with invoice date and amount.

kevin: Layout question: for org-level compact card, do we show per-project mini-bars in a collapsed flyout, or show a small stacked micro-chart inside the card? Micro-chart avoids modal but may be noisy.

marta: I'd prefer micro-chart inside card with ability to hover a legend to highlight project. Hover isn't great for touch though. On touch, tapping project name highlights it.

aria: billing-bot: "Invoice metadata now includes bill-run id and download URL. We'll surface in the UI API as invoice.download_url and invoice.run_id."

jess: Accessibility nit: make sure invoice download link has rel="noopener" and descriptive link text for screen readers. Avoid "click here".

sam: Small implementation note for frontend: charting lib needs to expose focusable datapoints for keyboard navigation. We can reuse the sparkline component but add tabindex and aria-describedby pointing to labels.

kevin: sample aria snippet for the sparkline: \n```html\n<svg role=\"img\" aria-label=\"Usage sparkline for last 30 days\">...</svg>\n<button aria-expanded=\"false\" aria-controls=\"breakdown-panel\">Expand</button>\n```

marta: Love it. One more copy thing: change "Token breakdown" header to "Token usage" — more action-oriented. Thoughts?

jess: "Token usage" reads better. Also add secondary copy under the header: "Hover or tap to see per-project details."

sam: For experiments, can we add a small toggle in settings for "Default to project-level on new accounts"? Some customers want that.

kevin: Add to product backlog. For the immediate task: mock up compact card with inline download on desktop, kebab menu on mobile, micro-chart, and aria adjustments.

marta: I'll update the figma and post new frames. Thanks all — will ping when ready for a quick design review. :thumbsup: 

kevin: :eyes:

jess: thanks!

aria: billing-bot: "Export job queued (ID: 6a7b). You will receive an email when ready."
